source_title: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 inhibition or deletion attenuates portal hypertension in rodents
summary_title: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 inhibition or deletion attenuates portal hypertension in rodents
executive_summary: This study investigated the effects of matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) inhibition or deletion on portal hypertension in rodent models. The research was motivated by the role of MMPs in extracellular matrix remodeling and angiogenesis, which are implicated in the development of portal hypertension. The study employed three experimental series: (1) rats with bile duct ligation (BDL) treated with minocycline, a nonselective MMP inhibitor; (2) BDL rats treated with SB-3CT, an MMP-2 and MMP-9 inhibitor; and (3) BDL mice with MMP-9 gene deletion. The primary findings revealed that both minocycline and SB-3CT significantly attenuated portal hypertension in BDL rats, as evidenced by reduced portal pressure (PP) and superior mesenteric artery (SMA) flow. Furthermore, MMP-9 knockout (KO) mice exhibited significantly lower PP compared to wild-type (WT) BDL mice. Minocycline decreased plasma vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) concentration and mesenteric protein expressions of MMP-9, inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), phospho-endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS), phospho-Akt, and phospho-VEGFR2. SB-3CT downregulated the expressions of phospho-SMAD2 and phospho-Erk. These results suggest that MMP-9 inhibition or deletion can alleviate portal hypertension and associated derangements. A key limitation is the lack of investigation into the specific mechanisms underlying the observed effects.
methodological_details: The study employed a combination of in vivo experiments using rodent models of liver cirrhosis. Male Sprague-Dawley rats (240-270 g) and male MMP-9 KO mice (C57BL/6 background) and their WT littermates were used. Biliary cirrhosis was induced in rats and mice via BDL. Rats were randomly assigned to receive minocycline (120 mg/kg/day, oral gavage), SB-3CT (0.16 mg/kg/day, i.p.), or vehicle for four weeks. MMP-9 KO mice and WT littermates underwent BDL or sham operations. Systemic and portal hemodynamics were measured using a PE-50 catheter and a multi-channel recorder. Mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate, and PP were continuously recorded. Cardiac output was measured by thermodilution. SMA flow was measured using a pulsed-Doppler flow transducer. SMA perfusion was performed using Krebs solution. Liver perfusion was performed using oxygenated Krebs solution. Portosystemic shunting was determined using color microspheres. Mesenteric angiogenesis was quantified using CD31-labelled microvascular networks. Liver fibrosis was assessed using Sirius red and H&E staining. Western blotting was used to analyze protein expression. Statistical analyses were performed using unpaired Student's t-tests or one-way ANOVA with LSD post-hoc tests, with a significance level of p < 0.05. The study was approved by the Taipei Veterans General Hospital Animal Committee (IACUC 2016-218).
procedures_architectures: The study utilized three experimental series. In the first series, BDL rats were treated with either minocycline (120 mg/kg/day, oral gavage) or vehicle. In the second series, BDL rats were treated with SB-3CT (0.16 mg/kg/day, i.p.) or vehicle. In the third series, MMP-9 KO mice and their WT littermates underwent BDL or sham operations. Hemodynamic measurements were performed using a PE-50 catheter connected to a Spectramed DTX transducer and a multi-channel recorder. SMA flow was measured using a pulsed-Doppler flow transducer. Cardiac output was measured by thermodilution. SMA perfusion was conducted using a modified in situ perfusion technique with Krebs solution. Liver perfusion was performed using an in situ system with oxygenated Krebs solution. Portosystemic shunting was assessed using color microspheres. Mesenteric angiogenesis was quantified using CD31 immunofluorescence. Liver fibrosis was evaluated using Sirius red and H&E staining. Western blotting was used to analyze protein expression. The study used a repeated measures design with multiple groups and treatments. The novelty lies in the investigation of MMP-9 inhibition or deletion specifically in the context of portal hypertension and the associated hemodynamic and angiogenesis changes.
key_results: Minocycline significantly reduced PP in BDL rats (p = 0.008), decreased SMA flow (p = 0.023) and CI (p = 0.002). Minocycline also significantly decreased plasma VEGF concentration (BDL-V vs. BDL-M: 16.71 ± 0.96 vs. 13.81 ± 0.73 ρg/ml, p = 0.028) and downregulated mesenteric protein expressions of MMP-9 (0.8043 ± 0.1676 vs. 0.3838 ± 0.0761, p = 0.033), iNOS (0.7789 ± 0.0806 vs. 0.5378 ± 0.0616, p = 0.030), phospho-eNOS (1.4287 ± 0.1357 vs. 0.9857 ± 0.1347, p = 0.034), phospho-Akt (1.0565 ± 0.0878 vs. 0.7928 ± 0.0776, p = 0.044) and phospho-VEGFR2 (1.6277 ± 0.2960 vs. 0.9717 ± 0.1181, p = 0.048). SB-3CT reduced PP (p = 0.019) and SMA flow (p = 0.003) in BDL rats. MMP-9 KO BDL mice had significantly lower PP compared with WT BDL mice (12.1 ± 0.5 vs. 7.8 ± 0.7 mmHg, p = 0.007). In the hepatic system, minocycline significantly decreased the liver fibrotic area. SB-3CT significantly downregulated the expressions of phospho-SMAD2 (1.3308 ± 0.0881 vs. 0.8536 ± 0.0817, p = 0.003) and phospho-Erk (0.6007 ± 0.0392 vs. 0.3424 ± 0.0353, p = 0.003).
